Anwar Hossain Madbar ------ Accused-Petitioner

State ------ Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: This Rule was issued on an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the opposite-party to show cause as to why the accused-petitioner Anwar Hossain Madbar should not be enlarged on bail in Sessions Case No. 13 of 2001 arising out of GR Case No. 227 of 1999 corresponding to Nariya Police Station Case No. 4 dated 15-6-2007 under sections 147/148/149/307/323/324/326/302/448/427/380 /114 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of Sessions Judge, Shariatpur. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that one Ramijuddin Makdam as informant on 8-6-1999 at 15-00 hours lodged a first information report with Nariya Police Station against 80 accused persons including the present petitioner and 10/15 others alleging, inter alia, that the accused persons being armed with deadly weapons such as revolver, pipegun, ramdao, etc. attacked his grandson named Jahangir Makdam while accused Anwar Hossain by his revolver fired at Jahangir Makdam who being injured fell down on the ground. At this stage accused Moru Makdam dealt a ramdao blow on the left leg of the victim Jahangir Makdam and accused Hafizur Rahman Mollik by his own gun fired at Jahangir Makdam while other accused persons simultaneously beat him. When the informant party came forward to rescue the victim the accused persons attacked them causing injury on the persons of Mijanur Rahman and Humayun Makdam and thereafter, the accused persons forcibly entered into the house of Jane Alam and looted valuable goods worth Taka 1,00,000 and thereafter, the accused persons left the place of occurrence while the victim Jahangir Makdam was shifted to Shariatpur Sadar Hospital for treatment, wherein the doctor on duty declared him dead. Upon the aforesaid first information report Nariya Police Station Case No. 4 dated 8-6-1999 under sections 147/148/149/307/323/324/326/302/448427/380/114 of the Penal Code was started. 

 4. In usual course the case record was sent to the Court of Sessions Judge, Shariatpur, wherein it was registered as Sessions Case No. 13 of 2001. Ultimately, the charge sheeted accused persons were put on trial in the Court of Sessions Judge, Shariatpur to answer a charge of the case under sections 448/427/395/326/302/34 of the Penal Code. 

 7. Mr Rafique-ul-Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner, after placing the first information report, charge sheet and deposition of witnesses, submits that the first information report was lodged against 80 accused persons and police after investigation submitted charge sheet against 72 accused on 29-2-2000 and the charge of the case was framed on 4-4-2002 and since then to till now the prosecution only examined 5 witnesses out of 41 charge-sheeted witnesses to prove its case. He further submits that the accused petitioner was arrested on 7-8-2003 and since then he has been languishing in jail custody and there being no prospect of early disposal of this case. 

 9. On the other hand, Mr Khandaker Diliruzzaman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State, opposes the Rule. He submits that there is specific allegation in the first information report against the petitioner and the case is now pending for trial and, as such, at this stage the accused-petitioner may not be enlarged on bail. 

 10. We have heard the learned Advocate as well as the learned Assistant Attorney-General, perused the application, supplementary affidavits and other connected documents as annexed therewith. It appears that earlier the present accused-petitioner filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7776 of 2006 before this Court for bail and on 27-8-2006 the said application was disposed of with a direction to conclude the trial within 4(four) months from the date of receipt of this order failing which the Court shall consider the prayer for bail of the petitioner and the said order was received on 30-11-2006. It also appears that the charge of the case was framed on 4-4-2002 and the prosecution by this time examined only 5(five) witnesses out of 41 charge-sheeted witnesses and they have stated nothing against this accused petitioner. It also appears that the informant is not an eye-witness and there is case and counter-case between the parties and 32 co-accused are on bail. It also appears that there is an unnecessary delay in holding trial of this case and there is no certainty when the rest witnesses will turn up to depose. 

 11. Since the prosecution has failed to show any cogent reason for not concluding the trial for a long time without any fault on the part of the accused in spite of direction of this Court dated 27-8-2006 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7775 of 2006 the learned Sessions Judge ought to have considered the bail prayer of the accused petitioner. 

 12. In the above facts and circumstances of the case vis-a-vis the direction of this Court dated 27-8-2006 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7775 of 2006, we are inclined to enlarge the accused petitioner on bail who has been in custody since 7-8-2003.
